gloss: to accept a loss silently; to give up without protest

definitions.gloss: to accept a loss silently; to give up without protest; to swallow one's grievance
definitions.explanation: To resign oneself to an unfair situation without taking action or complaining, usually because one feels powerless to change it.

examples.japanese: {泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}りするしかなかった。
examples.english: I had no choice but to accept it silently.

examples.japanese: {被害|ひがい}に{遭|あ}っても{泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}りする{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people who suffer harm just accept it without protest.

examples.japanese: {詐欺|さぎ}に{遭|あ}ったのに{泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}りせず、{警察|けいさつ}に{届|とど}けたほうがいい。
examples.english: If you've been scammed, rather than giving up silently, you should report it to the police.

notes:
{泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}り literally means "crying oneself to sleep" ({泣|な}く + {寝入|ねい}る), evoking the image of someone who can only cry and then fall asleep without resolving their problem. The expression conveys resignation in the face of injustice or mistreatment.

USAGE:
Used both as a noun ({泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}り) and as a suru verb. Often appears with しかない (have no choice but to) or せず (without doing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}りするしかない: have no choice but to accept it
- {泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}りせずに: without giving up quietly
- {泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}りさせない: not let someone be taken advantage of silently
- {消費者|しょうひしゃ}の{泣|な}き{寝入|ねい}り: consumers quietly accepting unfair treatment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {諦|あきら}める: to give up — more neutral; can be used for positive acceptance too
- {我慢|がまん}する: to endure; to put up with — emphasizes patience and endurance rather than resigned defeat
- {泣|な}く{泣|な}く: reluctantly; tearfully — an adverb describing doing something unwillingly
